abstract: The African Trypanosome (Trypanosoma brucei) persists in the mammalian host by periodically altering its surface coat with antigenically distinct versions of the Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG). This process is called antigenic variation and produces repeated cycles of immune clearance and parasite VSG switching, leading to high morbidity and mortality in the absence of chemotherapeutic intervention. Elucidating how variant VSGs evade immune clearance is thus central to understanding trypanosomiasis. Progress in studying the large repertoire of thousands of VSG proteins has been hindered by the challenge of producing these coat proteins. Here we report the use of suspension HEK293 cells for this purpose, a system with robust yields that preserves many key elements of VSG structure and post-translational modifications, verified by expressing, purifying, and determining the crystal structures of the well-characterized proteins VSG2 and VSG3. We then applied this heterologous expression system to the production of several VSGs that had failed to express natively in T. brucei, including truncated VSG-Related Proteins (VRPs) from T. brucei and VSGs from T. vivax. This allowed for the determination of the structures of the T. brucei VRP VSG1619 as well as the VSG F9WSW0 from Trypanosoma vivax (T. vivax). The structure of VSG1619 shows similarities to the upper-lobe structures of B-class VSGs, but the monomers do not assemble into either the typical A-class dimer or B-class trimer in solution or in the crystals. The structure of T. vivax F9WSW0 is notable as a divergent member of the Class-A group that was developed from structures of T. brucei VSGs, with a canonical dimer but differences in fold, disulfide placement, and N-linked glycosylation. The described expression system provides additional insight into the family of VRPs and opens the door to general progress with the VSGs of more divergent trypanosome species through recombinant protein production.

metadata.title: A recombinant expression system for the Variant Surface Glycoproteins enables structural elucidation of challenging classes of trypanosome proteins

summary: HEK293 expression system produces trypanosome VSG coat proteins, enabling crystal structures of VSG2, VSG3, a T. brucei VRP and a T. vivax VSG.
title: A recombinant expression system for the Variant Surface Glycoproteins enables structural elucidation of challenging classes of trypanosome proteins
